newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France pilots strike for third day.
newsitem.headline: Air France pilots strike for third day.

text.p: Air France pilots stayed on strike for a third straight day on Thursday, badly disrupting flights.
A spokesman for the French national airline said it cut short-haul flights by half and medium-haul flights by 30 percent, but maintained all scheduled long-haul flights.
In a war of figures, the pilots' union SNPL said 90 percent of short-haul flights were cancelled and the airline had to cancel all cargo flights in order to ensure long-haul flights.
The airline said it only cancelled one cargo flight on Tuesday and another on Thursday.

The stoppage, scheduled to end on Friday, two days before a parliamentary election, was called after talks broke down over the carrier's plans to pay new pilots between nine and 30 percent less than current crews, depending on experience.
SNPL said it would meet on Friday to make fresh proposals to the management.

The airline planned to implement the new pay scale in a merger with its short-haul arm Air Inter Europe, intended to make them more efficient as European airlines are opened up to cross-border competition.

In another protest, French dairy farmers stopped trucks and dumped thousands of litres (gallons) of milk after government-sponsored talks failed to end a row with milk processors and distributors over falling prices.
Police said protesters emptied a truck carrying 17,000 litres (3,800 gallons) of milk in the eastern Vesoul region and there were two other incidents in western France.
Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur accused milk processors of blocking a deal to freeze prices in Wednesday's four-hour talks with dairy farmers and distributors.

Vasseur called the emergency talks after dairy farmers had blocked deliveries to hypermarkets in various parts of France on Tuesday to draw public attention to a gradual slide in milk prices they say threatens their jobs.
In another dispute on farm prices, police and justice have been told to crack down on farmers attacking Spanish fruit and vegetable trucks in southern France, French officials said.

A Spanish truck driver was in hospital in Montpellier and two French farmers were in custody after attacks earlier this week by farmers who want tighter controls on imported produce cheaper than their own.
